correctness.rationale: Ideals of a finite product of fields are indexed by subsets of the factor set, multiplication corresponds to support intersection, and nonzero annihilating ideals are exactly the nonempty proper supports. The three distance cases are exhaustive and mutually exclusive. The pair counts follow by inclusion-exclusion and surjection counting, and direct algebra gives the Wiener formula.

Guo–Wu–Yu (2017) proves that products of fields give finite Boolean graphs and studies structural/clique/coloring properties; full-text searches found no occurrence of 'Wiener' or 'Hosoya'.
Asir et al. (2022) explicitly names annihilating-ideal graphs as a remaining platform for Wiener-index work.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The known exact formulas and the known structural identification do not imply a published distance enumerator in the inspected sources; the present result combines the structural model with a new exact count.

value.rationale: The result gives the complete distance distribution, not only a single index, for every finite semisimple commutative ring with at least two simple factors. It directly answers a named 2022 research direction on Wiener indices of annihilating-ideal graphs for a canonical infinite ring family, and the formula is uniform and independent of field sizes.
